data.name: Dhatri
data.gender_notes: Dhatri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dhatri is a goddess of giving, associated with fertility and abundance. She is often depicted with a pot of rice or grains, symbolizing her role as a giver and nurturer. The name Dhatri carries the meaning “Goddess of Giving” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Dhatri usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of giving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Dhatri represents the divine feminine energy of giving, nurturing, and abundance. She is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all beings and the importance of giving and receiving in the cycle of life.
data.etymology: Dhatri belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Giving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhatri total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Dhatri, as a name, carries the rich essence of the Hindu tradition, which places immense importance on giving, sharing, and nurturing. This name represents the selfless and generous nature of the divine and inspires those who bear it to follow in the footsteps of the goddess by being givers and nurturers themselves, fostering love, compassion, and kindness in their communities and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dhatri signifies one's deep connection to the divine as a giver and nurturer. It is a reminder of one's duty to give, to share, and to nourish not only the physical world but also the spiritual world. With the name Dhatri, one receives a divine blessings, inspiring an everlasting longing to give generously and to be a living embodiment of the essence of the divine, the eternal giver and nurturer.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dhatri represents the nurturing and life-giving force of the universe. As a mother provides sustenance to her child, Dhatri bestows essential blessings and resources upon those she cares for. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'dhatu,' meaning 'element' or 'substance,' reflecting her role in providing the fundamental building blocks of life.

vedic_reference.note: Dhatri is a form of the goddess Lakshmi, the Hindu goddess of wealth, fortune, and prosperity.
